key_insight: Specialized, physics-driven ML force fields are needed to make machine-learning interatomic potentials reliable for complex materials dynamics beyond near-equilibrium chemistry.
engineering_relevance: For fracture, interfaces, multiphase evolution, and open systems, the right force field must be tuned and validated against the specific observable of interest rather than judged only by general benchmark accuracy.
method: Compare universal equivariant foundation models with task-specific specialized potentials
Address out-of-distribution reactive states using physics-guided adaptations
Evaluate trade-offs in sampling, nonlocality, and computational cost across demanding dynamical settings
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes four challenging application contexts—electrified interfaces, open systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture—to benchmark MLIP design against intended observables.
watch_item: High-order architectures and specialized adaptations can be computationally expensive and may still fail if strained or reactive configurations are underrepresented in training data.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
